product: Merck is a science-led biopharma: oncology led by KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX ($8.4B in Q2 2026, including $463M QLEX), plus WELIREG and Lynparza and Lenvima alliances; vaccines (GARDASIL, CAPVAXIVE, VAXNEUVANCE, ProQuad); cardiometabolic and respiratory (WINREVAIR, OHTUVAYRE, Adempas); infectious disease (BRIDION, PREVYMIS); diabetes (JANUVIA, declining); and animal health ($1.8B).
demand: Q2 2026 sales rose 5% (4% ex-FX), driven by demand-led oncology growth in earlier-stage indications, 75% WINREVAIR growth and launch uptake, and 8% animal health growth. Partly offset by generic-driven diabetes declines, lower US vaccine demand and weak LAGEVRIO.
pricing_power: Mixed and worsening on mature drugs: positive net pricing in US vaccines and BRIDION, but lower net pricing in JANUVIA, JANUMET, Lenvima and VAXNEUVANCE, plus US most-favored-nation pricing commitments and higher managed-care rebates. Novel first-in-class launches such as WINREVAIR and LIPFENDRA carry stronger pricing.
competition: Intense across the board: SCLC (I-DXd versus other 2L options), diabetic macular edema (remigromig versus ranibizumab and Eylea), PCSK9 (oral LIPFENDRA versus injectables), PD-1 franchise (Opdivo, Imfinzi, Tecentriq, Libtayo), vaccines (Pfizer, GSK), animal health (Zoetis, Elanco) and HIV (Gilead).
team: Led by chairman and chief executive Robert M. (Rob) Davis, who cites nearly 70 years in cardiovascular disease and the pipeline transformation. About 21% of employees worldwide are covered by collective bargaining agreements; 2025 voluntary turnover was about 4.8%.
market_strategy: Transform the portfolio away from KEYTRUDA dependence before the late-2020s patent cliff via science-led business development and first-in-class modalities: the Terns acquisition ($5.7B charge), the October 2025 Verona Pharma acquisition adding OHTUVAYRE, Blackstone R&D funding, and an investor event at ESMO 2026 to showcase the pipeline.
bull: Six broker raises in 90 days (HSBC 150->172, Leerink 127->161, Wolfe 155->180) and a 2026-10-10 I-DXd PDUFA plus 2026-10-26 ESMO event give dated catalysts; WINREVAIR volume +75% to $588M.
bear: Q2 2026 GAAP loss $0.54/sh, gross margin 73.5% from 77.5%, FY26 EPS guided $2.66-2.76 vs $8.98; BRUNELLO eye bleeding/inflammation flag; Citi $125, RBC and TD Cowen Hold; KEYTRUDA -1%.
falsifier: I-DXd fails to win FDA approval on the 2026-10-10 PDUFA date, or Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-29 show FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance cut below $2.66.
web_what_changed: 2026-08-04 Q2 2026 sales $16.6B up 5%; FY2026 sales guidance raised to $66.3-67.3B but non-GAAP EPS cut to $2.66-2.76 on a $2.31/share Terns charge. FDA approved LIPFENDRA (enlicitide), first once-daily oral PCSK9 inhibitor. 2026-08-19 first positive Phase 3 individualized mRNA cancer vaccine (intismeran plus KEYTRUDA) in melanoma. September: Japan subcutaneous KEYTRUDA, WINREVAIR label expansion, BRUNELLO DME win, Alzheimer trial stopped.
web_not_known_yesterday: 2026-09-24 pivotal Phase 2b/3 BRUNELLO showed remigromig (MK-3000) non-inferior to ranibizumab in diabetic macular edema but flagged higher eye bleeding and inflammation rates. 2026-09-24 WINREVAIR label expanded with Phase 3 HYPERION data for recently diagnosed PAH. 2026-09-24 Merck discontinued another Alzheimer trial under the Neuphoria partnership.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume and demand led. Growth came from oncology demand in earlier-stage indications, WINREVAIR volume up 75% to $588M, WELIREG up 67%, CAPVAXIVE up 42%, plus animal health demand. Mix turned negative where generics and net price bite: JANUVIA down 31%, VAXNEUVANCE down 35%, LAGEVRIO down 95%; KEYTRUDA fell 1% globally.
web_suppliers: FY2025 10-K: raw materials obtained from numerous suppliers worldwide; most principal materials are multi-sourced, but certain raw or intermediate materials come primarily from only one source, mitigated by inventory and supplier management. No supplier disclosed as currently constrained. Key development partners include Daiichi Sankyo (I-DXd), Kelun-Biotech (sac-TMT), Gilead (HIV) and Moderna (mRNA-4157).
web_customers: Highly concentrated. Merck sells mainly to drug wholesalers and retailers, hospitals, government agencies and managed care. Largest accounts receivable at 2025-12-31 were McKesson 22%, Cencora 21% and Cardinal Health 13% of total receivables; there is no disclosed offsetting diversification of this US distributor dependence.
web_who_loses: If Merck wins: injectable PCSK9 makers Amgen (Repatha), Regeneron/Sanofi (Praluent) and Novartis (Leqvio) face oral LIPFENDRA; ranibizumab and Eylea-based DME incumbents Roche and Regeneron face remigromig; 2L SCLC chemotherapy and rival PD-1 and ADC players face I-DXd if approved 2026-10-10; generic JANUVIA makers already take share.
web_contradicting_evidence: Q2 2026 GAAP loss $0.54 per share, net loss $1.34B, gross margin down to 73.5% from 77.5%, R&D $9.7B on a $5.7B Terns charge; FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guided $2.66-2.76 versus $8.98 in 2025. BRUNELLO carried an eye-safety red flag on bleeding and inflammation. Citi holds $125 and TD Cowen and RBC hold. Another Alzheimer trial was scrapped 2026-09-24.
web_if_management_right: FY2026 worldwide sales land at $66.3-67.3B, I-DXd is approved on 2026-10-10 as a first-in-class B7-H3 ADC in 2L ES-SCLC, and launches (LIPFENDRA, WINREVAIR, OHTUVAYRE, WELIREG, sac-TMT, intismeran) scale before the KEYTRUDA loss of exclusivity around 2028. Consensus models EPS recovering toward roughly $9.53 in FY2027; Merck hosts an investor event at ESMO 2026 on 2026-10-26.
web_if_management_wrong: Earnings break first: FY2026 non-GAAP EPS is guided near $2.74 with gross margin already at 73.5%, so any launch miss leaves the 2028 KEYTRUDA patent cliff unhedged. KEYTRUDA is $8.4B of a $16.6B quarter, so QLEX conversion and earlier-stage indications must keep working. BRUNELLO eye safety or an I-DXd regulatory setback would remove two of the largest offsets.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Daiichi Sankyo (4568) shares I-DXd economics; Kelun-Biotech supplies sac-TMT; Gilead co-develops islatravir and lenacapavir; Moderna partners on intismeran autogene mRNA-4157; Blackstone Life Sciences funds R&D. Distributors McKesson, Cencora and Cardinal Health gain volume, and ADC and mRNA contract manufacturers and CROs benefit from the expanded pipeline.
